title: Compare with the Previous Row Using LAG
learning_objective: Learn how to compare each log row with the row immediately before it.

tutorial.explanation: LAG reads a value from a previous row without joining the table to itself. It is useful when the meaning of a row depends on its neighbor in an ordered sequence.
tutorial.syntax: SELECT id, num, LAG(num) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS previous_num FROM logs;
tutorial.mental_model: ORDER BY lines up the rows. LAG then lets each row look one step backward.

guided_example.prompt: Show each log row with the previous num value.
guided_example.solution_query: SELECT id, num, LAG(num) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS previous_num FROM logs ORDER BY id;
guided_example.explanation: The first row has no previous value, so previous_num is NULL. Every later row can see the num from the row before it.

practice.prompt: Return rows where num is the same as the previous row's num.
practice.expected_query: WITH compared AS (SELECT id, num, LAG(num) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS previous_num FROM logs) SELECT id, num FROM compared WHERE num = previous_num ORDER BY id;

hints: Put the window calculation in a CTE.
